records.title: Twelve Easy Pieces
records.context_note: An educational selection of Handel keyboard pieces, prepared for piano by Hans von Bülow. This external listing documents the same named collection; it is not a history of one single composition.

records.title: Four Impromptus
records.context_note: Schubert wrote his four D. 899 impromptus in 1827. Their lyricism and improvisatory character made them central works of Romantic piano repertoire.

records.title: Franz Liszt: Original Works and Transcriptions for the Piano (publisher catalog)
records.notes: Photograph appears to show a price list / advertisement, not the identifiable front cover of an individual score. Catalog separately until linked to the physical score.
records.context_note: This photograph seems to show a publisher list rather than an individual score cover. The links offer background on Liszt’s large output of original piano works and arrangements, not identification of a specific piece.

reference_links.label: Library of Congress · Liszt published music

records.title: Cantata Profana
records.context_note: Bartók’s dramatic cantata draws on a Romanian folk-ballad tale of nine brothers transformed into stags. The choral and orchestral writing connects folklore with his modern compositional language.

records.title: The Harmonica-Player (from “Alley Tunes: Three Scenes from the South”)
records.context_note: “The Harmonica Player” is the final number of David W. Guion’s suite Alley Tunes, drawing on musical representations of the American South. The linked university collection identifies the piece in Guion’s surviving manuscripts.

reference_links.label: University of Texas · Guion manuscript collection

records.title: 35 Sonatas for Piano
records.context_note: Domenico Scarlatti composed hundreds of compact keyboard sonatas known for rhythmic energy and inventive keyboard writing. This volume collects a selection; its individual contents need to be checked against the score.

reference_links.label: Piano Library · Scarlatti sonatas, Longo numbering

records.title: Bagatelles
records.context_note: Beethoven’s bagatelles are short piano pieces that range from intimate miniatures to concentrated late-style experiments. His principal published sets include Opp. 33, 119 and 126.

records.title: Franz Liszt: Original Works for the Piano (publisher catalog)
records.notes: Appears to be a publisher listing/pricelist; the title of the physical score (if any) is not shown.
records.context_note: This cover image is a publisher list and does not identify one Liszt work. The reference discusses original piano works, transcriptions and how they appeared in published editions.

records.title: Forty-Eight Preludes and Fugues
records.publisher: Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music
records.notes: Book I and Book II are printed on the cover; photographed volume not established. Appears in at least three photographs (IMG_0454, IMG_0501, IMG_0511). Whether they are separate physical copies needs checking.
records.context_note: Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier contains two books of 24 preludes and fugues each, one pair in every major and minor key. This was an influential exploration of keyboard composition and counterpoint.

records.title: Piano Compositions by Russian Composers (publisher catalog, Series One)
records.notes: This is a catalog listing works by several Russian composers, rather than an identifiable individual score cover.
records.context_note: The photographed page appears to be a publisher catalog for Russian piano repertoire, not one composition. The references give broader historical context rather than a work identification.

reference_links.label: Library of Congress · Russian music collections
University of Maryland · Russian piano music study

records.title: Klavierübung I. Teil — Partiten Nr. 1–3
records.notes: Urtext edition. Peters number looks like 4598a; confirm from physical copy.
records.context_note: Bach’s six keyboard partitas were issued separately from 1726 and gathered as the first Clavier-Übung volume in 1731. This printed score contains Partitas Nos. 1–3.

records.title: Chromatic Fantasy and Fugue; Concerto in the Italian Style; Fantasy in C Minor; Prelude and Fugue in A Minor
records.context_note: This anthology brings together several separate Bach keyboard works. The linked essays cover the Chromatic Fantasia and Fugue and the Italian Concerto; they should not be read as a description of every piece in this volume.

records.title: Fifteen Two-Part Inventions
records.notes: Cover states “Analyzed, Edited & Phrased by James Friskin.”
records.context_note: Bach’s fifteen two-part inventions were designed to cultivate clear, independent voice leading and musical expression. They remain fundamental keyboard teaching pieces.

records.title: Englische Suiten — Nos. 1–3 (English Suites)
records.notes: Urtextausgabe; Peters plate/edition number should be checked.
records.context_note: Bach’s six English Suites belong to the Baroque suite tradition, assembling stylized dance movements. This score covers the first three suites.

records.title: First Lessons in Bach
records.context_note: First Lessons in Bach is an edited instructional anthology rather than a single composition. The linked catalog describes the same teaching collection and its history.

reference_links.label: University of Rochester · First Lessons in Bach
Google Books · First Lessons in Bach, Book 2

records.title: Fifteen Two-Part Inventions
records.context_note: This edition presents Bach’s fifteen two-part inventions, which combine the teaching of keyboard technique with the art of writing independent melodic voices.

records.title: Scenes from Childhood
records.context_note: Schumann composed Kinderszenen (Scenes from Childhood), Op. 15, in 1838. These are recollections of childhood expressed through short piano character pieces, not exercises intended only for children.

records.title: Messe in E-Moll
records.notes: Cover describes an edition for eight-part mixed choir and wind orchestra or organ; “Orgelauszug” appears on cover.
records.context_note: Bruckner’s Mass No. 2 in E minor was first composed in 1866 for eight-part choir and wind instruments. This cover appears to show a vocal or organ-reduction edition, which differs from the original forces.

records.title: The Art of the Fugue
records.context_note: The Art of Fugue is Bach’s late exploration of contrapuntal possibilities built from a common musical subject. Its incomplete surviving state has prompted much study of Bach’s intentions.

records.title: Preludes
records.context_note: Chopin’s 24 Preludes, Op. 28, form a cycle across all major and minor keys. The form lets him concentrate a distinct mood and musical idea into each short piece.

records.title: Sonaten (Sonatas)
records.context_note: Chopin wrote three piano sonatas across different stages of his career. The widely known B-flat-minor Sonata includes the Funeral March; the exact works in this edition should be checked in its contents.

records.title: Second Concerto
records.context_note: Rachmaninoff’s Second Piano Concerto, Op. 18, was completed in 1901 following a difficult creative period. It became one of his best-loved works for its expansive lyrical themes.

records.title: Ten Preludes
records.context_note: The Ten Preludes of Rachmaninoff’s Op. 23 were composed in the early twentieth century and range from intimate reflection to brilliant piano writing.

records.title: Horn-Trio in E-flat Major
records.notes: “Es-dur – E♭ major – Mi♭ majeur” on cover.
records.context_note: Brahms wrote his Horn Trio in E-flat, Op. 40, in 1865, the year of his mother’s death. Its unusual combination of horn, violin and piano evokes a distinctive, often elegiac sound.

records.title: Konzert in F Minor (Piano Concerto)
records.notes: Title and opus visible; score format/arrangement should be confirmed by checking inside.
records.context_note: Chopin composed his F-minor concerto, later published as Piano Concerto No. 2, around 1829. It was written before the E-minor concerto that received the lower published number.

records.title: Ballades
records.context_note: Chopin’s four ballades helped establish a new kind of self-contained, dramatic piano narrative. Their musical stories do not correspond to one agreed literary program.

records.title: Nocturnes
records.context_note: Chopin transformed the nocturne into an expressive piano genre of lyrical melodies and elaborate ornament. His examples build on the earlier nocturnes of John Field.

records.title: Waltzes
records.context_note: Chopin’s waltzes reimagine the familiar dance as sophisticated piano miniatures, many intended for listening rather than ballroom dancing.

records.title: Impromptus
records.context_note: Chopin’s four impromptus are polished piano compositions whose titles suggest spontaneity. The celebrated Fantaisie-Impromptu was issued only after his death.

reference_links.label: Henle · Chopin Impromptus and their history

records.title: Sonaten (Sonatas)
records.notes: Edition Peters number appears to be 488b; confirm from original.
records.context_note: Schubert’s piano sonatas range from early classical models to expansive late Romantic-era predecessors. This volume contains only a selection; specific D-numbers require a contents check.

records.title: Forty-Eight Preludes and Fugues
records.publisher: Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music
records.notes: Book I and Book II appear on the cover. Compare IMG_0454 and IMG_0511 to determine whether same physical score or multiple copies.
records.context_note: The Forty-Eight Preludes and Fugues is another edition of Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier. It contains two books, each exploring all 24 major and minor keys.

records.title: Album-Leaves
records.context_note: Albumblätter (Album Leaves), Op. 124, gathers twenty short Schumann piano pieces. Many were composed earlier and then brought together as a published collection.

records.title: Concerto in D Minor
records.context_note: Mozart’s Piano Concerto No. 20 in D minor, K. 466, dates from 1785. Its minor-key drama later appealed to Romantic-era pianists and composers.

records.title: The “Goldberg” Variations
records.notes: Centennial Edition stated on the cover.
records.context_note: The Goldberg Variations, BWV 988, unfold an aria, thirty variations and a return of the aria. They are among Bach’s most celebrated large-scale keyboard compositions.

records.title: Variations, Rondos and Other Works for Piano
records.notes: Publisher and edition details not readable on front cover.
records.context_note: Mozart’s solo keyboard output includes variations on popular melodies as well as rondos and independent pieces. This anthology spans multiple works rather than a single named composition.

records.title: Complete Shorter Works for Solo Piano
records.notes: Cover lists Waltzes Op. 39; Klavierstücke Op. 76, 118, 119; Rhapsodies Op. 79; Fantasies Op. 116; Intermezzi Op. 117; and other pieces.
records.context_note: This compilation spans shorter Brahms piano works, including the late pieces of Opp. 116–119, often notable for inward, songlike writing. A complete match to the anthology contents still needs checking.

records.title: Sonaten (Sonatas)
records.notes: Edition Peters number appears to be 488a; confirm from physical copy.
records.context_note: This is another volume of Schubert’s piano sonatas. Some of these works remained unfinished or unpublished in his lifetime; the specific sonatas in this printing need checking.

records.title: Toccatas
records.context_note: Bach’s seven keyboard toccatas, BWV 910–916, explore an improvisatory style with virtuoso passages and contrasting contrapuntal sections.

records.title: Polonaises
records.context_note: Chopin’s polonaises transform a Polish dance rhythm into works of display, reflection and national association. The genre spans much of his composing life.

records.title: Complete Preludes & Etudes for Solo Piano
records.context_note: The préludes are concise character pieces covering all 24 keys, while Chopin’s études combine technical challenges with expressive musical invention. This anthology brings together both genres.

records.title: Forty-Eight Preludes and Fugues
records.publisher: Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music
records.notes: Book I and Book II appear on cover. Compare IMG_0454 and IMG_0501 before declaring separate physical copies.
records.context_note: Another photograph of an edition of Bach’s Well-Tempered Clavier. The 48 preludes and fugues can be studied as both a teaching tradition and a landmark of contrapuntal music.

records.title: Well-Tempered Clavier
records.context_note: Book II of the Well-Tempered Clavier contains a second series of 24 preludes and fugues in every major and minor key, assembled around 1742.

records.title: Sonatas for Pianoforte
records.publisher: Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music
records.editor: Harold Craxton; Donald Francis Tovey (commentary and notes)
records.context_note: Beethoven’s piano sonatas form a body of works spanning his early, middle and late styles. This is a printed collection of sonatas, not a single composition.

records.title: An die Freude
records.notes: Cover states “Klavier-Auszug”; exact vocal/scoring arrangement is not established from the cover.
records.context_note: “An die Freude” (Ode to Joy) is associated with Schiller’s poem and Beethoven’s choral setting in the Ninth Symphony. The photographed piano reduction needs checking to establish exactly which passage or arrangement it contains.

records.title: Préludes
records.notes: Cover gives “préludes ... (1er Livre)”; imprint not legible from this photo.
records.context_note: Debussy’s Préludes, Book I, contains twelve vividly characterized piano pieces, including “The Girl with the Flaxen Hair” and “The Sunken Cathedral.” The evocative titles hint at images rather than literal musical stories.

records.title: Symphonic Studies
records.context_note: Schumann’s Symphonic Études, Op. 13, transform a theme through a sequence of concert studies and variations. Differences among published versions make the edition history particularly interesting.

records.title: Fantasia
records.context_note: Schumann’s Fantasie in C major, Op. 17, grew from a tribute connected to Beethoven and became one of his most ambitious solo piano works, with a strongly Romantic emotional character.

records.title: Sonatas
records.context_note: Beethoven’s 32 mature piano sonatas are a central part of the keyboard repertoire. This book is one volume of an edited collection, and its exact sonatas need to be confirmed from the contents.
